q: 1. The angle of intersection of a curve is the angle between
options: prolongation of back tangent and forward tangent
explain: The angle of intersection is the angle between the prolongation of the back (rear) tangent and the forward tangent, measured at the point of intersection of the two straights.

q: 2. Setting out of a simple curve by two theodolite method does not require ...............
explain: The two-theodolite method allows for curve setting using only angular intersection, meaning no chaining (linear measurement) along the curve is needed.

q: 3. The curve composed of two arcs of different radii having their centers on the opposite side of the curve, is known ...............
explain: A reverse curve (S-curve) consists of two circular arcs bending in opposite directions with centers on opposite sides of the common tangent.

q: 4. Point of tangency is the ...............
options: common point where the radius changes
common point where the radius and direction changes
explain: The Point of Curve (PC) is the start, and the Point of Tangency (PT) is the end of the curve where it joins the forward tangent.

q: 5. In a simple curve, 'External distance' is the distance between ...............
options: vertex and middle point of the curve
vertex and the centre of the curve
point of curve and point of tangency
explain: The external distance (apex distance) is the distance from the intersection point (vertex) to the apex of the curve.

q: 6. The approximate formula for radial or perpendicular offsets from the tangent is
explain: For short distances (x), the perpendicular offset (O) is approximately $O = x^2 / 2R$.

q: 7. Perpendicular offset from a tangent to the junction of a transition curve and circular curve is equal to
explain: In the geometry of a transition curve, the offset at the end of the transition curve (where it meets the circular curve) is four times the shift 's'.

q: 8. If D is the angle of deflection of a simple curve of radius R, the length of its long chord, is
explain: The long chord is the straight line connecting the start and end of the curve. Its length is calculated as $2R sin(Delta/2)$, where $Delta$ (or D) is the deflection angle.

q: 9. The chord of a curve less than peg interval, is known as
explain: A sub-chord is any chord shorter than the standard 'normal' chord length (usually the peg interval).

q: 10. An ideal transition curve is .............
explain: The clothoid (or Euler spiral) is considered the ideal transition curve because its curvature increases linearly with distance.

q: 11. A simple circular curve is designated by the
options: angle subtended at the centre by a chord of any length
angle subtended at the centre by a chord of a particular length
explain: A simple circular curve is conventionally designated by its 'degree of curve', which is the angle subtended at the centre by a chord of one particular standard length (e.g., 30 m or 100 ft).

q: 12. The degree of the curve is the angle subtended by a chord of length.
explain: As per this text's convention, the degree of a curve is defined as the angle subtended at the centre by a standard chord length of 30 m.

q: 13. When R is the radius of the curve (in meters), D is the degree of curve (in degrees) and length of the chord is 30 m, then the relation between R and D is
explain: For a 30 m chord definition of degree of curve, the standard relation is R = 1720/D (approximately, derived from R = (chord/2)/sin(D/2) for small D).

q: 14. A deflection angle is
options: more than 90 deg but less than 180 deg
equal to the difference between the angle of intersection and 180 deg
equal to the difference between the angle of intersection and 360 deg
explain: The deflection angle and the angle of intersection are supplementary, so the deflection angle equals 180 deg minus the angle of intersection.

q: 15. When the length of a chord is less than the peg interval, it is known as
explain: A chord shorter than the standard peg interval (used typically at the beginning or end of a curve) is called a sub-chord.

q: 16. The total length of the curve is equal to
explain: The length of a circular curve (arc) subtending an angle phi (in degrees) at the centre, with radius R, is given by L = pi*R*phi/180.

q: 17. 'Point of curve' is
explain: The 'point of curve' refers to the point of commencement of the curve, i.e., where the curve begins (tangent point at the start).

q: 18. An ideal vertical curve to join two gradients, is
explain: A simple parabolic curve is considered ideal for vertical curves joining two different road/rail gradients, since it provides a constant rate of change of grade.

q: 19. A simple circular curve is designated by .............
options: angle subtended at the centre by a chord of any length
angle subtended at the centre by a chord of particular length
explain: In engineering practice, a curve is often designated by the degree of the curve, which is the angle subtended at the center by a standard chord (usually 20m or 30m).

q: 20. The 'point of curve' of a simple circular curve is .............
explain: The point of curve (PC) is the point where the straight alignment (tangent) ends and the circular curve begins; it is the point of commencement.

q: 21. The angle between the back tangent and forward tangent of a curve is
explain: The central angle (or angle of intersection) is the angle between the two tangents at the point of intersection (PI).

q: 22. If the radius of a simple curve is R, the length of the chord for calculating offsets by the method of chords produced, should not exceed .............
explain: For the method of chords produced, the chord length is generally kept within R/20 to ensure that the approximation (arc length ≈ chord length) remains accurate for plotting.

q: 23. A deflection angle is .............
options: equal to the difference between the angel of intersection and 180°
equal to the difference between the angel of intersection and 360°
explain: The sum of the deflection angle and the internal angle of intersection ($I$) equals 180°. Therefore, Deflection Angle = $180° - I$.

q: 24. An angle of deflection right, may be directly obtained by setting the instrument to read .............
explain: If you zero the instrument on the back sight and then turn to the next station, the resulting clockwise reading is the deflection angle.

q: 25. The shift of a curve is equal to .............
explain: The 'shift' is the distance by which the circular curve must be moved inward to accommodate the transition curve, calculated as $S = L^2 / (24R)$.

q: 26. The polar equation for a lemniscate curve is .............
explain: The Bernoulli's Lemniscate is defined by the polar equation $r^2 = a^2 \cos 2\theta$ (or $l = k \sqrt{\cos 2\theta}$ in this context).

q: 27. A lemniscate curve between the tangents is transitional throughout, if the polar deflection angle of its apex is equal to .............
explain: For a fully transitional lemniscate curve, the polar deflection angle at the end is exactly one-sixth of the total deflection angle $\phi$.

q: 28. A lemniscate curve will not be transitional throughout, if its deflection angle, is .............
explain: The lemniscate loses its specific transition properties once the deflection angle reaches or exceeds $45°$.
